errors.discriminating_probe: Give a composite whose inner derivative is not one and ask the student to point to the factor that came from inside.
errors.name: Inner derivative omitted from a chain rule application
non_conceptual_causes: copying slip when the inner function is linear
time pressure on a routine step
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the outer function correctly and stops, leaving the derivative of the inner function out of the product.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong, and in a multipart question the error propagates into every later part that uses it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to list the layers before differentiating and to tick each one as its derivative is written.
errors.name: One layer of a multi-layer composite left undifferentiated
non_conceptual_causes: losing track of the layers under time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A composition of three functions is differentiated through the first two layers and the innermost derivative is omitted.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong; no credit is available for a partially applied rule in a single answer item.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the inner function first, as a separate question, before the derivative is requested.
errors.name: Outer derivative read at the input rather than at the inner output
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the row or the axis
errors.observed_behavior: In a table or graph based composite, the derivative of the outer function is read at the stated input instead of at the value the inner function produces.
errors.scoring_consequence: The numerical answer is wrong even though the chain rule structure was written correctly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the chain rule symbolically before any number is substituted.
errors.name: Table entries combined by addition rather than by the chain rule
non_conceptual_causes: confusion with the sum rule under time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response adds the two tabulated derivatives instead of multiplying them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student where on the displayed graph the derivative fails to exist before any value is requested.
errors.name: Slope read at a point where a graph is not differentiable
non_conceptual_causes: the corner is close to a grid line
errors.observed_behavior: A slope is reported at a corner or a cusp of a supplied graph as though the derivative existed there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is wrong, and the response misses that the correct answer is that the derivative does not exist.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the outermost operation before writing any derivative.
errors.name: Product or quotient rule omitted when a composite is one factor
non_conceptual_causes: the outer structure is read after the inner one under time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The composite factor is differentiated correctly but the enclosing product or quotient rule is not applied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong; in the 2025 implicit differentiation task the product rule carries its own scoring point (sg-25:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate a single y term on its own and to say why the extra factor appears.
errors.name: A term in y differentiated without the dy/dx factor
non_conceptual_causes: the factor is written on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: In an implicit differentiation the y terms are differentiated as though y were the independent variable, so no dy/dx factor appears.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiation is not eligible for the completely correct differentiation point described in the Chief Reader reports (crabbc-25:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate the mixed term alone and to name the rule used.
errors.name: Product rule omitted on a term containing both variables
non_conceptual_causes: the term is short and is treated as a single symbol
errors.observed_behavior: A term that is a product of an expression in x and an expression in y is differentiated as though one of the two were constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiation loses the point for a completely correct implicit derivative, and the 2025 scoring guidelines award the product rule its own point (sg-25:20, crabbc-25:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the d/dx operator on both sides before any term is differentiated.
errors.name: Right hand side of the equation dropped after differentiating
non_conceptual_causes: notation shorthand carried over from a differentiation exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the left hand side and omits the equals zero or the derivative of the right hand side, leaving an expression rather than an equation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader report for 2025 records that responses dropping the equals zero were generally unable to recover and earned neither of the first two points (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark every occurrence of dy/dx in the differentiated equation before any algebra is done.
errors.name: dy/dx terms divided before they are collected
errors.observed_behavior: The response divides by a factor while dy/dx still appears on both sides, so the isolated expression is not dy/dx.
errors.scoring_consequence: The stated expression for dy/dx does not match the verification requested, and later parts built on it are compromised.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name every variable appearing in the expression for dy/dx before substituting.
errors.name: Only one coordinate substituted into dy/dx
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the x coordinate into an expression containing both variables and reports a slope still containing y.
errors.scoring_consequence: No numerical slope is produced, so the evaluation point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state what the slope of a vertical line is before the curve is considered.
errors.name: Horizontal and vertical tangent conditions exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the words horizontal and vertical
errors.observed_behavior: The denominator of dy/dx is set to zero when a horizontal tangent is requested, or the numerator when a vertical tangent is requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported point is wrong and the reasoning point is not available.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student whether the candidate point lies on the curve, as a separate question.
errors.name: Tangent condition satisfied but the point is not checked against the curve
non_conceptual_causes: the check is done mentally and not written
errors.observed_behavior: A coordinate satisfying the condition on dy/dx is reported as a point of the curve without substituting it into the defining equation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader reports record responses failing to connect dy/dx with the defining equation, which costs the point for the coordinates (cr-23:23, cr-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student what goes wrong with the formula when the original derivative is zero.
errors.name: Inverse derivative rule stated without its nonzero hypothesis
non_conceptual_causes: the hypothesis is treated as understood
errors.observed_behavior: The formula for the derivative of an inverse is written with no mention that the derivative of the original function at the matching input must not be zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point that requires the hypothesis is not earned; the Chief Reader reports record unverified hypotheses as a recurring loss (BC-ERR-99008).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the matching input as a separate step before the reciprocal is taken.
errors.name: Inverse derivative evaluated at the given value rather than at the matching input
non_conceptual_causes: a table row exists at the given value, inviting a misread
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the reciprocal of the derivative of the original function at the value supplied, instead of at the input whose output is that value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is wrong although the formula is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the two columns before any arithmetic is done.
errors.name: Reciprocal of the function value reported instead of the reciprocal of the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: misread of which table column is which
errors.observed_behavior: The response inverts the value of the original function rather than the value of its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to derive one of the formulas from the corresponding trigonometric equation.
errors.name: Inverse trigonometric derivative formula recalled incorrectly
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of the inverse sine is used for the inverse tangent, or a sign or a radical is misplaced in the recalled formula.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong from the first line.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the inner expression as a single letter before substituting it into the formula.
errors.name: Inner expression not substituted throughout an inverse trigonometric formula
non_conceptual_causes: the inner expression is short and is skipped
errors.observed_behavior: The standard formula is written with the variable rather than the inner expression in the denominator, or the inner derivative factor is omitted.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong; the missing factor is the chain rule element the formula requires.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state the outermost operation and the rule it requires before differentiating.
errors.name: Rule chosen from the surface appearance of the expression
errors.observed_behavior: A product rule is applied to a composite, or a power rule to an exponential, because the expression resembles that family at a glance.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is wrong from the first step; the Chief Reader report for 2022 records rule choice by shape as an observed behaviour (cr-22:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student whether the unsimplified form already answers the question.
errors.name: Unnecessary simplification introduces an algebra error
errors.observed_behavior: A correct derivative is simplified further and the simplification changes the value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader reports record unnecessary simplification as a recurring source of lost points (cr-24:19, crabbc-25:26).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the order requested at the top of the work before differentiating.
errors.name: Differentiation stopped one order short of the order requested
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the first derivative where the second was asked for, or the second where the third was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although every differentiation performed is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read their own line aloud and say what each symbol names.
errors.name: Higher-order derivative notation written incorrectly
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes dy in place of dy/dx, or uses dy/dx where the operator d/dx is meant, or mixes the two notations inside one line.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 Chief Reader report lists this notation as a misconception seen in implicit differentiation responses, and poor notation cost points there (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to list every quantity that must be known before the substitution is made.
errors.name: First derivative value not substituted into the second derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the first derivative is computed on scratch work and not carried over
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the second derivative containing dy/dx is evaluated without first computing the value of dy/dx at the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The numerical second derivative is wrong, although the product and chain rule points described in the 2025 scoring guidelines may still be earned (sg-25:20).
